housing_pipeline.description: The proposal is to erect a new 13-unit, seven-story building on a vacant lot utilizing the California State Density Bonus. The project will provide up to seven parking spaces, including one accessible van parking space, and 14 bicycle parking spaces (13 Class I and one Class II). The requested waivers are private open space, height limit, rear yard, and sun access plane. The requested incentives and concessions include parking maximum limits and bay window projection per Planning Code Section 136. The project would require approximately 35 cubic yards of excavation.

Demolition of two existing non-historic, one-story buildings with basements. The existing buildings house post-secondary educational facilities and no housing. Per SB 423, the proposed building will be approximately 114,341 gross square feet with nine stories and a basement. There are 120 proposed units with 39.2% two-bedroom units and the remainder will be one-bedroom units.

The Revised Flower Mart Project would include the demolition of ten existing buildings and associated parking lots, and construction of five new buildings up to 270 feet in height (up to 18 stories) containing 2,660,700 square feet of office/laboratory space, 100,000 square feet of retail/commercial space, and 300,000 square feet of cultural, institutional, and educational (CIE) space. The proposed project would also include installation of approximately 827 off-street vehicular parking spaces, 10 freight loading spaces, and 625 bicycle parking spaces.

The project sponsor is proposing three variants to the proposed project: a Residential (Variant 1), a Mixed-Use (Variant 2), and an Institutional (Variant 3). 

Under the Residential Variant, there would be seven buildings with a maximum height of 500 feet. Approximately 100,000 square feet of retail/commercial space and 3,214,000 square feet of residential space would accommodate approximately 3,500 dwelling units. The Residential Variant would not include dedicated office or CIE space. This variant would provide approximately 1,800 vehicular parking spaces, 14 freight loading spaces, and approximately 1,200 bicycle parking spaces. 

Under the Mixed-Use Variant, there would be five buildings with a maximum height of 480 feet. The Mixed-Use Variant would include approximately 100,000 square feet of retail/commercial space; 1,130,000 square feet of residential space to accommodate approximately 1,242 dwelling units; and 1,493,600 square feet of office/laboratory space. This variant would not include dedicated CIE space. The Mixed-Use Variant would provide approximately 1,115 vehicular parking spaces, 10 freight loading spaces, and approximately 825 bicycle parking spaces. 

Under the Institutional Variant, there would be five buildings with a maximum height of 270 feet. This variant would include approximately 100,000 square feet of retail/commercial space; 1,273,600 square feet of office/laboratory space; and 1,387,200 square feet for either CIE or medical space. Two existing curb cuts on 7th Street and one existing curb cut on Langton Street would be removed. Four new street trees would be added along the 7th Street (three trees) and Langton Street (one tree) frontages.

The Project proposes to demolish the existing non-historic office building and construct a new 42-story, approximately 444-foot tall building featuring 392 dwelling units above approximately 4,000 square feet of ground-floor retail. Off-street vehicle parking and loading facilities will be provided, as will Class 1 and 2 bicycle parking. The Project is utilizing the Individually-Requested State Density Bonus Program to achieve a density bonus thereby maximizing residential density on the Site.

The Project includes demolition of an existing two-story industrial building (measuring approximately 21,630 square feet (sq ft)) and new construction of a seven-story-with-basement, 80-ft tall, residential building (measuring approximately 144,487 gross square feet (gsf)) with 200 dwelling units and 125 Class 1 bicycle parking spaces. The Project does not possess any off-street vehicular parking, and is requesting an on-street loading space and two on-street car-share parking spaces. The dwelling unit mix includes six one-bedroom units, 94 two-bedroom units, and 100 two-bedroom units with two dens. The Project includes approximately 11,840 sq ft of open space through below-grade outdoor areas along 12th Street and Norfolk Streets (collectively measuring 1,732 sq ft), an interior courtyard (measuring approximately 3,978 sq ft), two private open areas on the second floor (collectively measuring 523 sq ft) and two rooftop decks (collectively measuring 5,607 sq ft). The Project also includes streetscape improvements including sidewalk widening, street trees, planting strips and ten Class 2 bicycle parking spaces. The Project would also merge and subdivide the two existing lots into three new lots, which would result in a project site with 199.99-ft of frontage along Norfolk Street and 157-ft of frontage along 12th Street, and a lot area of 25,518 sq ft. Pursuant to California Government Code Sections 65915-65918, the Project Sponsor has elected to utilize the State Density Bonus Law.
